A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Moiré video authentication work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting and additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original real-video recordings, physics-based simulations, generated-video attacks, correlation measurements, and ROC analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds simulations testing alternative grating layouts, rotation, and oblique viewing in Appendix C.2.

M1.justification: The grating prototype and ArUco tracking, FFT phase extraction, PnP compensation, and sliding-window correlation pipeline are retained. Appendix C.2 applies the same verifier separately to simulated fringe regions; it does not specify a new fusion algorithm or replace the main method.

E1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds simulated scenarios with orthogonal fringe regions, rotated tags, 45-degree viewing/motion, and compound board rotation. This broadens geometric input conditions within the existing authentication task; the real-video population and generative attack coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate the same generative attack models: Veo 3.1, Grok Imagine, and LTX-2. Newly discussed MoiréTracker and MoiréVision are related-work citations, not experimentally evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The added simulations specify 120-, 180-, and 240-frame sequences, separate axis evaluation, and rotation-compensation choices. Table 3 reports mean and range of 30-frame window correlations alongside whole-sequence correlation. Existing real/AI evaluation and ROC protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.2, Figure 15, and Table 3 introduce a dedicated geometric robustness study covering multi-directional patterns, rotated-tag trajectories, oblique motion, and compound rotation. This substantially extends the diagnostic evidence beyond v1's original motion/distance validation and threshold analysis.

E5.justification: Table 3 introduces explicit within-video variability reporting through minimum–maximum window correlations. Appendix C.2 also describes window standard deviations, although their values are omitted. Existing group standard deviations, Welch's test, and Cohen's d are unchanged; no increase in repeated runs or seed reporting is established.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds results for the new simulated conditions: mean window correlations are 0.951/0.854 for orthogonal regions and 0.667/0.570 under compound rotation. These supplement, rather than revise, existing results. Real/AI mean correlations remain 0.87/0.57, and ROC AUC remains 0.8453.

T1.justification: The optical derivation, translation/rotation reasoning, correlation invariant, and equations are retained. v2 adds attribution to classical Moiré theory and descriptions of standard correlation summaries, without a new proof, formal assumption, or mathematical correction.

C1.justification: The abstract and first contribution change 'derive' to 'utilize' the invariant as a verification criterion, but the derivation claim remains in the conclusion. The substantive claims about passive authentication, physical coupling, empirical separation, and threat analysis retain their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 newly attributes degradation under compound rotation to axis cross-talk, perspective distortion, and contrast variation. It interprets slant chiefly as reduced signal quality and proposes fusion, reliability filtering, and low-contrast rejection. Existing face-swap, static-scene, and physics-based forgery limitations remain.

D1.justification: The new simulations document sequence lengths, evaluated regions/axes, rotation-compensation status, and score aggregation. These are additional reproducibility details for the added tests, although precise trajectories and combined-decision logic remain unspecified. Existing assembly instructions, assets, and generation prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds MoiréTracker and MoiréVision and discusses them alongside the previously cited MoiréBoard. The new paragraph distinguishes authentication through correlation from motion/pose recovery, while Section 2.1 more explicitly acknowledges classical optical foundations.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 5. v2 also adds keywords and acknowledgements, adjusts headings and contribution wording, and updates appendix signposting. Most existing prose and the overall scientific narrative are retained.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column formatting, with extensive figure and table resizing and relocation. Prompt figures occupy separate pages, ROC and threshold plots become side-by-side, and the passive/active comparison moves to Related Work. Figure 15 and Table 3 are new displays.

improvement.justification: The added geometric robustness evidence and clearer comparison with prior Moiré sensing work improve understanding of applicability and positioning. The gain is limited: the new tests are simulations, and Table 3 omits the standard-deviation and decision outputs promised in its accompanying text. The core method and principal authentication results remain unchanged.
